gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-exa: Existence has round lowercase counters like wide glass portholes, giving every word an industrial look. Lexend Exa follows in a plain sans with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, so extended reading stays smooth and open.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-giga: Industrial and a bit mechanical, Existence cuts its terminals well short of the bowl. Lexend Giga sits beside it in flat, single-weight lines with generous tracking, giving each word room while the heading carries the weight.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with a single nib, its body height nearly matching the capitals. And Existence does the louder work, its porthole counters and short-cut terminals giving headings an industrial bite that the friendlier sans-serif leaves alone.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-peta: Approachable is the first word for Lexend Peta, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed c shapes, a big x-height and curves that never thin out. Existence adds an industrial edge.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, one line weight and open curves on every round letter. Existence earns its keep big and short, where its porthole counters and clipped terminals can show off.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta is wide and widely tracked. Existence stamps out industrial headings with terminals cut short of the bowl, while the sans below uses tall-bodied small letters and constant-width strokes to keep things approachable.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-montserrat-alter: Contemporary in feel, Montserrat Alternates has a c as open as a bent paperclip and lowercase crowding toward the capital line. Existence, the industrial heading above it, hands over to a body that moves steadily.
gen-dafont-forza-fs-bespoke-serif: Forza crowds its glyphs together like beads pressed on a wire. Bespoke Serif then arrives with dignified thick and thin strokes, its thin lines about half the weight of the thick, so rod-stock precision gives way to something more authoritative.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-gambetta: Galaxy sets dense, tall lowercase with loose letterfit, and its arches are as thick as the stems beside them. But Gambetta brings a gentler, bookish text serif, whose mild taper and moderate height take the pressure off.
gen-dafont-galaxy-lora: Commanding yet cosmic, Galaxy stands tall in its lowercase with loose, spacious letterfit. And Lora, a bookish serif with a broad c and modest hairline thinning, keeps a long read feeling literary and unhurried.
